description.en-US: The human reference, unique within its organization. Immutable: it is quoted to the vendor on the RFQ and must still identify the same document after confirmation, because an RFQ and the order it becomes are one record (BR 5.1, 55.1).

The business lifecycle, and nothing else. It carries no received, billed or paid value: those belong to Inventory and to Payment, and mirroring them here would let this copy disagree with the module that owns the fact (BR 6, 55.2-55.5). Written only by the lifecycle actions, never by a plain update, so no transition can happen without its audit event (PUR-R3, PUR-R6).

The supplier. A plain ulid with no edge: the party belongs to Contacts, and a foreign key across a module boundary would make Purchase's schema depend on Contacts' table. Validated through a port, which checks the party has an active vendor profile rather than merely existing.
The vendor's own number for this order, as quoted back by them.
Where the order came from, when it was raised on behalf of something else.

What every amount on this order is denominated in. A plain ulid: the currency belongs to Essential. There is no exchange-rate model, so one order is in one currency and the totals never cross currencies; the currency's decimal_places is what the computed totals are rounded to.
When the quotation must be answered by.
When the goods are expected. Defaulted from the vendor's lead time at confirmation when it is not stated.
When the order was confirmed. Written by the confirm action alone: it is the evidence that a commitment was made at a particular moment, so a client that could set it could backdate a purchase.
The agreement this order draws against, when it does. Optional: most orders are one-off.
Set when this order is one of several alternatives being compared for the same requirement. The group is a technical record with no business meaning of its own (BR 28).

Whether the order is closed to editing. A boolean and NOT a status value: an order can be locked in more than one status, and folding it into status would multiply the states and lose the distinction between confirmed-and-editable and confirmed-and-locked (BR 7, 55.2). Written by the lock and unlock actions, and by confirm when the organization's policy is auto_lock.

Whether the vendor has confirmed receipt of the order. Written by the acknowledge action alone: it is a statement about what the counterparty did, so a buyer being able to set it would make it worthless as evidence (BR 22).

Sum of the lines before tax. System-computed and never accepted from a client, so that the total cannot disagree with what it totals: the lines are what a reader can verify, so the lines win (BR 10.2, 55.12).

Sum of the lines' tax. Each line's tax is supplied by the client rather than calculated: there is no tax engine in this system and the requirement forbids building one here, so the server sums what it is given.
Untaxed plus tax. Stored rather than computed on read so that the approval threshold comparison and the total-range filter stay plain SQL instead of a per-row computation.

Whether this order needed approval, decided at confirmation from the organization's approval mode and threshold. Recorded rather than re-derived on read, because the policy may change afterwards and the question of whether this order needed approval when it was confirmed must keep its original answer.
Who approved it. Written by the approve action alone: a client that could set this could approve its own order.
